name: Mantra Health
one_liner: Virtual therapy, psychiatry and DBT-based self-care for college students, free through schools that partner with Mantra Health.
best_for: Students at a college or university that partners with Mantra Health
Students facing waits at the campus counseling center
Students who want DBT-based self-care skills between sessions
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who are not enrolled at a partner school
Students who need more sessions than their school covers and can't self-pay
short_description: Schools sponsor Mantra Health so enrolled students can get virtual therapy, psychiatry and self-care programs, usually at no cost.
long_description: Mantra Health works with colleges and universities to offer students virtual mental health care. Students sign up with their school email; depending on what the school has turned on, they can use self-care content (one school's program is built on DBT skills: mindfulness, emotion regulation, distress tolerance and interpersonal effectiveness) and see a licensed provider after a care assessment. The school pays, so most services are free to students, but clinical sessions are capped each year and extra sessions can be self-paid. Mantra providers work with the campus counseling center, and students' health information is protected under HIPAA, according to a partner school's FAQ. We found no published study of Mantra's service.

pricing.notes: Paid for by the partner school. Clinical sessions are capped per year; a self-pay option exists for extra sessions (price not published).

privacy.notes: Care records are protected under HIPAA per a partner school's FAQ, and the App Store listing reports no tracking; we could not open Mantra's own privacy policy to confirm advertising or sale practices.

faqs.q: Is Mantra Health free for students?
faqs.a: If your college partners with Mantra, services are typically free or heavily subsidized for enrolled students. The school pays for the partnership. Check with your campus counseling center or student health to see if Mantra is available.

faqs.q: How do I know if my college has Mantra?
faqs.a: Check with your campus counseling center, student health services, or search for mental health resources on your school's website. Mantra partners with over 100 institutions. Your school should promote available resources during orientation.

Mantra provides individual therapy, group therapy, psychiatric medication management, crisis support, and self-care tools. Services are delivered virtually by licensed providers who specialize in working with college students.

faqs.q: How does Mantra work with campus counseling?
faqs.a: Mantra supplements campus counseling centers rather than replacing them. Students with immediate or complex needs may see campus counselors, while Mantra provides overflow capacity and specific services. The systems coordinate to serve students better.

patient_summary: If your school partners with Mantra Health, you create an account with your school email and can use self-care tools or book a care assessment with a licensed provider by video. Your school pays, so most services are free, though the number of clinical sessions each year is capped. Ask your counseling center whether your school offers Mantra.

availability.note: Only for students enrolled at partner colleges and universities; features depend on what each school has enabled.
